DSPM helps you discover, protect, and investigate sensitive data risks across your digital estate by unifying Microsoft Purview Information Protection with other Microsoft Purview solutions and capabilities. With a focus on data security objectives with guided workflows that offer default sensitivity labels, default policies, and more, DSPM helps you monitor, assess, and remediate data risks regardless of where sensitive data resides. ## Licensing Microsoft Purview Information Protection capabilities are included with Microsoft Purview. The licensing requirements can vary even within capabilities, depending on configuration options. To identify licensing requirements and options, see the [Microsoft Purview service description](/en-us/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description). ## Know your data ![Know your data for Microsoft Purview Information Protection solution overview](media/knowyourdata-mipsolution.png) Knowing where your sensitive data resides is often the biggest challenge for many organizations. Microsoft Purview Information Protection data classification helps you to discover and accurately classify ever-increasing amounts of data that your organization creates. Graphical representations help you gain insights into this data so you can set up and monitor policies to protect and govern it. | Step | Description | More information | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | Describe the categories of sensitive information you want to protect. You already have an idea of what types of information are most valuable to your org and what types aren't. Work with stakeholders to describe these categories that are your starting point. | [Learn about sensitive information types](sit-sensitive-information-type-learn-about)
[Learn about trainable classifiers](trainable-classifiers-learn-about) | | 2 | Discover and classify sensitive data. Sensitive data in items can be found by using many different methods that include default DLP policies, manual labeling by users, and automated pattern recognition using sensitive information types or machine learning. | [Classifiers overview](data-classification-overview) | | 3 | View your sensitive items. Use content explorer and activity explorer for a deeper analysis of sensitive items and the actions that users are taking on these items. | [Get started with content explorer](data-classification-content-explorer)
[Get started with activity explorer](data-classification-activity-explorer) | ## Protect your data ![Protect your data for Microsoft Purview Information Protection solution overview](media/protect-mipsolution.png) Use the information from knowing where your sensitive data resides to help you more efficiently protect it. However, there's no need to wait—you can start to protect your data immediately with a combination of manual, default, and automatic labeling. Then, use [content explorer](data-classification-content-explorer) and [activity explorer](data-classification-activity-explorer) from the previous section to confirm what items are labeled and how your labels are being used. | Step | Description | More information | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | Define your [sensitivity labels](sensitivity-labels) and policies that will protect your organization's data. In addition to identifying the sensitivity of content, these labels can apply protection actions such as content markings (headers, footers, watermarks), encryption, and other access controls.[Example sensitivity labels](default-sensitivity-labels-policies#default-sensitivity-labels): **Personal** **Public** **General** - **Anyone (unrestricted)** - **All Employees (unrestricted)** **Confidential** - **Anyone (unrestricted)** - **All Employees** - **Trusted People** **Highly Confidential** - **All Employees** - **Specific People**[Example sensitivity label policy](default-sensitivity-labels-policies#default-sensitivity-label-policy): 1. Publish all labels to all users in the tenant 2. Default label of **General \ All Employees (unrestricted**) for items 3. Users must provide a [justification](media/sensitivity-label-justification-required.png) to remove a label or lower its classification | [Get started with sensitivity labels](get-started-with-sensitivity-labels)[Create and configure sensitivity labels and their policies](create-sensitivity-labels)[Restrict access to content by using sensitivity labels to apply encryption](encryption-sensitivity-labels) | | 2 | Label and protect data for Microsoft 365 apps and services. Sensitivity labels are supported for Microsoft 365 Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams meetings, and also containers that include SharePoint and OneDrive sites, and Microsoft 365 groups. Use a combination of labeling methods such as manual labeling, automatic labeling, a default label, and mandatory labeling. [Example configuration for client-side auto-labeling](default-sensitivity-labels-policies#client-side-auto-labeling): 1. Recommend **Confidential \ Anyone (unrestricted)** if 1-9 credit card numbers 2. Recommend **Confidential \ All Employees** if 10+ credit card numbers -- [typical end user experience, and the user selects the button to show sensitive content (Word only)](media/sensitivity-label-recommended.png)[Example configuration for service-side auto-labeling](default-sensitivity-labels-policies#service-side-auto-labeling): Apply to all locations (Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive) 1. Apply **Confidential \ Anyone (unrestricted)** if 1-9 credit card numbers 2. Apply **Confidential \ All Employees** if 10+ credit card numbers 3. Apply **Confidential \ Anyone (unrestricted)** if 1-9 US personal data and full names 4. Apply **Confidential \ All Employees** if 10+ US personal data and full names | [Manage sensitivity labels in Office apps](sensitivity-labels-office-apps)[Enable sensitivity labels for files in SharePoint and OneDrive](sensitivity-labels-sharepoint-onedrive-files)[Enable co-authoring for files encrypted with sensitivity labels](sensitivity-labels-coauthoring)[Configure a default sensitivity label for a SharePoint document library](sensitivity-labels-sharepoint-default-label)[Automatically apply a sensitivity label to Microsoft 365 data](apply-sensitivity-label-automatically)[Use sensitivity labels to protect collaborative workspaces (groups and sites)](sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites)[Use sensitivity labels to protect calendar items, Teams meetings, and chat](sensitivity-labels-meetings)[Use sensitivity labels with Microsoft Loop](sensitivity-labels-loop)[Use sensitivity labels to set the default sharing link for sites and documents in SharePoint and OneDrive](sensitivity-labels-default-sharing-link)[Apply a sensitivity label to a model in Microsoft Syntex](/en-us/microsoft-365/contentunderstanding/apply-a-sensitivity-label-to-a-model)[Sensitivity labels in Power BI](/en-us/power-bi/admin/service-security-sensitivity-label-overview) | | 3 | Discover, label, and protect sensitive items that reside in data stores in the cloud (Box, GSuite, SharePoint, and OneDrive) by using [Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](/en-us/cloud-app-security/what-is-cloud-app-security) with your sensitivity labels. [Example configuration for a file policy](/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/use-case-information-protection#prerequisites): Looks for credit card numbers in files stored in a Box account, and then applies a sensitivity label to identify the highly confidential info and encrypt it. | [Discover, classify, label, and protect regulated and sensitive data stored in the cloud](/en-us/cloud-app-security/best-practices#discover-classify-label-and-protect-regulated-and-sensitive-data-stored-in-the-cloud) | | 4 | Discover, label, and protect sensitive items that reside in data stores on premises by deploying the [information protection scanner](deploy-scanner) with your sensitivity labels. | [Configuring and installing the information protection scanner](deploy-scanner-configure-install) | | 5 | Auto-apply sensitivity labels in Microsoft Purview Data Map to discover and label items for Azure Blob Storage, Azure files, and Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2. | [Learn about sensitivity labels in Microsoft Purview Data Map](data-map-sensitivity-labels) | If you're a developer who wants to extend sensitivity labels to line-of-business apps or third-party SaaS apps, see [Microsoft Information Protection (MIP) SDK setup and configuration](/en-us/information-protection/develop/setup-configure-mip). ### Additional protection capabilities Microsoft Purview includes additional capabilities to help protect data. Not every customer needs these capabilities, and some might be superseded by more recent releases. Refer to the [Protect your data with Microsoft Purview](information-protection) page for the full list of protection capabilities. ## Prevent data loss ![Prevent data loss for Microsoft Purview Information Protection solution overview](media/dlp-mipsolution.png) Deploy Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies to govern and prevent the inappropriate sharing, transfer, or use of sensitive data across apps and services. These policies help users make the right decisions and take the right actions when they're using sensitive data. | Step | Description | More information | | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | Learn about DLP. Organizations have sensitive information under their control, such as financial data, proprietary data, credit card numbers, health records, and social security numbers. To help protect this sensitive data and reduce risk, they need a way to prevent their users from inappropriately sharing it with people who shouldn't have it. This practice is called data loss prevention (DLP). | [Learn about data loss prevention](dlp-learn-about-dlp) | | 2 | Plan your DLP implementation. Every organization will plan for and implement data loss prevention (DLP) differently, because every organization's business needs, goals, resources, and situation are unique to them. However, there are elements that are common to all successful DLP implementations. | [Plan for data loss prevention](dlp-overview-plan-for-dlp) | | 3 | Design and create a DLP policy. Creating a data loss prevention (DLP) policy is quick and easy, but getting a policy to yield the intended results can be time consuming if you have to do a lot of tuning. Taking the time to design a policy before you implement it gets you to the desired results faster, and with fewer unintended issues, than tuning by trial and error alone. [Help prevent sharing credit card numbers through email](dlp-create-policy-cc-email#help-prevent-sharing-credit-card-numbers-through-email): Prevents emails being sent if they contain credit card numbers or the email has a specific sensitivity label that identities highly confidential info. | [Design a DLP policy](dlp-policy-design)
[DLP policy reference](dlp-policy-reference)

[Create and deploy data loss prevention policies](dlp-create-deploy-policy) | | 4 | Tune your DLP policies. After you deploy a DLP policy, you'll see how well it meets the intended purpose. Use that information to adjust your policy settings for better performance. | [Create and deploy data loss prevention policies](dlp-create-deploy-policy) | ## Deployment strategies The credit card number examples are often helpful for initial testing and end user education. Even if your organization doesn't typically need to protect credit card numbers, the concept of these being sensitive items that need protection is easily understood by users. Many websites provide credit card numbers that are suitable for testing purposes only. You can also search for sites that provide credit card number generators so that you can paste the numbers into documents and emails. When you're ready to move your automatic labeling and DLP policies into production, change to classifiers and configurations that are suitable for the type of data used by your organization. For example, you might need to use trainable classifiers for intellectual property and specific types of documents, or exact data match (EDM) sensitive information types for privacy data that's related to customers or employees. Or, you might want to start by discovering and protecting IT-related information that is frequently the target of security attacks. Then, supplement this by checking for and preventing the sharing of passwords with DLP policies for email and Teams chat: - Use the trainable classifiers **IT** and **IT Infra and Network Security Documents** - Use the built-in sensitive info type **General Password** and create a custom sensitive info type for "password is" for the different languages used by your users Deploying an information protection solution isn't a linear deployment but iterative, and often circular. The more you know your data, the more accurately you can label it, and prevent data leakage. The results of those applied labels and policies flow into the [Reports](purview-reports) and tools, which in turn makes more sensitive data visible for you to protect. Or, if you're already protecting that sensitive data, consider whether it requires additional protective actions. You can start to manually label data as soon as you've defined sensitivity labels. The same classifiers that you use for DLP can be used to automatically find and label more data. You can even use sensitivity labels as a classifier, for example, block sharing items that are labeled highly confidential. Most customers already have some solutions in place to protect their data. Your deployment strategy might be to build on what you already have, or focus on gaps that offer the most business value or addresses high risk areas. To help you plan your unique deployment strategy, reference [Get started with sensitivity labels](get-started-with-sensitivity-labels) and [Plan for data loss prevention](dlp-overview-plan-for-dlp). ### Consider a phased deployment You might prefer to deploy information protection by using a phased deployment that implements progressively restrictive controls. This approach gradually introduces new protection measures for users as you gain familiarity and confidence with the technology. For example: - From default labels and no encryption, to recommending labels that apply encryption when sensitive data is found, and then automatically applying labels when sensitive data is found. - DLP policies that progress from auditing oversharing actions, to more restrictive blocking with warning to educate users, and then blocking all sharing. Details of such a phased deployment might look something like the following plan, where sensitivity labels and DLP policies become more integrated with each other to provide greater data protection than if they were used independently: ![Conceptual graphic for a phased deployment where sensitivity labels and DLP policies become more integrated and the controls more restricted.](media/information-protection-phased.png) # [Phase 1](#tab/phase-one) Sensitivity label configurations: - **General\All Employees**: Default label for email. No encryption. If applied on emails, block users from over-sharing. - **Confidential\All Employees**: Default label for documents. No encryption. If applied on emails, block users from over-sharing. - **Highly Confidential\All Employees**: No encryption. If applied on emails, block users from over-sharing. DLP policy A: - If 1-2 instances of credit cards are found, block external sharing except if the item is labeled as **Personal** or **Confidential\Anyone (unrestricted)**. Use logging and reporting for analysis. DLP policy B: - If 3-9 instances of credit cards are found, block external sharing, cloud egress, and copy to removable drives except if the item is labeled as **Confidential\Anyone (unrestricted)**. Use logging and reporting for analysis. DLP policy C: - If 10+ instances of credit cards are found, block external sharing, cloud egress, and copy to removable drives with no exceptions. Use logging and reporting for analysis. # [Phase 2](#tab/phase-two) Sensitivity label configurations: - **General\All Employees**: Default label for email. No encryption. If applied on emails, block users from over-sharing. - **Confidential\All Employees**: Default label for documents. Encryption with Full Control to all employees. If applied on emails, block users from over-sharing. - **Confidential\Trusted People**: Encryption that lets users assign permissions with Encrypt-Only for Outlook and prompts users in Word, PowerPoint, and Excel. If applied on emails, display DLP tooltip to warn users that unauthorized users won't be able to read the email. - **Highly Confidential\All Employees**: Encryption with Full Control to all employees. If applied on emails, block users from over-sharing. Recommend the label if 3-9 instances of credit cards are found with high confidence, or 10+ instances of credit cards are found with low confidence. DLP policy A: - If 1-2 instances of credit cards are found, block external sharing except if the item is labeled as **Personal** or **Confidential\Anyone (unrestricted)**. Send an alert on repeat actions in a short period of time. DLP policy B: - If 3-9 instances of credit cards are found, block external sharing, cloud egress, and copy to removable drives except if the item is labeled as **Confidential\Anyone (unrestricted)**. Send alert on repeat actions over time. DLP policy C: - If 10+ instances of credit cards are found, block external sharing, cloud egress, and copy to removable drives with no exceptions. Report on each individual action. # [Phase 3](#tab/phase-three) Sensitivity label configurations: - **General\All Employees**: Default label for email. No encryption. If applied on emails, block users from over-sharing. - **Confidential\All Employees**: Default sublabel for the parent label or label group, **Confidential**. Encryption with all usage rights except Export and Full Control to all employees. Encryption with Full Control usage rights to managers. Recommend the label if 1-9 instances of credit cards are found with low confidence. - **Confidential\Trusted People**: Encryption that lets users assign permissions with Encrypt-Only for Outlook and prompts users in Word, PowerPoint, and Excel. If applied on emails, display DLP tooltip to warn users that unauthorized users won't be able to read the email. - **Highly Confidential\All Employees**: Encryption with all usage rights except Export and Full Control to all employees. Encryption with Full Control usage rights to managers. Recommend the label if 1-9 instances of credit cards are found with low confidence. If applied on emails, block users from over-sharing. Automatically apply the label if 3-9 instances of credit cards are found with high confidence, or 10+ instances of credit cards are found with low confidence. - **Highly Confidential\Specific People**: Encryption that lets users assign permissions with Do Not Forward for Outlook and prompts users in Word, PowerPoint, and Excel. Exception for all DLP blocking rules. DLP policy A: - If 1-2 instances of credit cards are found, block external sharing except if the item is labeled as **Personal**, **Confidential\Trusted People**, or **Highly Confidential\Specific People**. Send an alert on repeat actions in a short period of time. DLP policy B: - If 3-9 instances of credit cards are found, block external sharing, cloud egress, and copy to removable drives except if the item is labeled as **Confidential\Anyone (unrestricted)** or **Highly Confidential\Specific People**. Send alert on repeat actions over time. DLP policy C: - If 10+ instances of credit cards are found, block external sharing, cloud egress, and copy to removable drives with no exceptions. Report on each individual action. DLP policy D: - If sensitivity labels of either **General\All Employees**, **Confidential\All Employees**, or **Highly Confidential\All Employees** block external sharing with policy tip and no exceptions. --- Configuration details for this example phased deployment: - [Default sublabel for a parent label or label group](sensitivity-labels-office-apps#specify-a-default-sublabel-for-a-parent-label-or-label-group) - [Data loss prevention Exchange conditions and actions reference](dlp-exchange-conditions-and-actions) - [Confidence levels and other elements of a sensitivity type](sit-sensitive-information-type-learn-about#fundamental-parts-of-a-sensitive-information-type) - [Use sensitivity labels as conditions in DLP policies](dlp-sensitivity-label-as-condition) - [Encryption that lets users assign permissions](encryption-sensitivity-labels#let-users-assign-permissions) - [Encryption for specific usage rights](encryption-sensitivity-labels#assign-permissions-to-specific-users-or-groups) - [Configure and view alerts for data loss prevention policies](dlp-configure-view-alerts-policies) For other deployment guidance that includes a phased deployment strategy, see [Secure by default with Microsoft Purview and protect against oversharing](/en-us/purview/deploymentmodels/depmod-secure-by-default-intro) from our Product Engineering team. ## Training resources Interactive guides: [Microsoft Purview Information Protection](https://mslearn.cloudguides.com/guides/Protect%20sensitive%20data%20with%20Microsoft%20Purview%20Information%20Protection) Learning modules for consultants and admins: - [Introduction to information protection and data lifecycle management in Microsoft Purview](/en-us/training/modules/m365-compliance-information-governance) - [Classify data for protection and governance](/en-us/training/modules/m365-compliance-information-classify-data) - [Protect information in Microsoft Purview](/en-us/training/modules/m365-compliance-information-protect-information) - [Prevent data loss in Microsoft Purview](/en-us/training/modules/m365-compliance-information-prevent-data-loss) To help train your users to apply and use the sensitivity labels that you configure for them, see [End-user documentation for sensitivity labels](get-started-with-sensitivity-labels#end-user-documentation-for-sensitivity-labels). When you deploy data loss prevention policies for Teams, you might find the following end-user guidance useful as an introduction to this technology. It includes some potential messages that users might see: [Teams messages about data loss prevention (DLP) and communication compliance policies](https://support.microsoft.com/office/teams-messages-about-data-loss-prevention-dlp-and-communication-compliance-policies-c5631c3f-f61b-4306-a6ac-6603d9fc5ff0).

Research task (read-only; do not write any files). Today is 2026-11-05. I am building a catalogue of "what must be done before what" for Microsoft 365 security configuration (an ordered dependency graph of changes). Load WebSearch and WebFetch with ToolSearch (query "select:WebSearch,WebFetch", max_results 2) and use them. Prefer learn.microsoft.com and official GitHub. Find the CURRENT URL of each page (many have moved; e.g. Defender docs now live under learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/, /defender-for-identity/, /defender-cloud-apps/, /defender-office-365/). Note: WebFetch on learn.microsoft.com returns the whole page as markdown with YAML front matter, which is large, so fetch only the pages you need. A cheaper way to read just the front matter is Bash: `curl -sL <url> | grep -oE '<meta name="(ms.topic|ms.date|original_content_git_url)" content="[^"]*"'`.

Sources to cover:
1. Microsoft 365 Business Premium setup and security guides (the "secure your business data with Business Premium" / top 10 ways / security deployment guide for Business Premium; find the current URLs).
2. Defender for Endpoint deployment guide (plan, prepare, set up, onboard, configure; find the current URL).
3. Defender for Identity prerequisites (sensor requirements, Directory Service account, auditing / event collection, etc.).
4. Defender for Cloud Apps deployment (get started / quick start; app connectors, Cloud Discovery, Conditional Access app control, and its integrations with Defender for Endpoint and Entra Conditional Access).
5. Exchange Online: modern authentication (and disabling Basic auth / SMTP AUTH), and mail-flow security guidance (e.g. connectors, enhanced filtering for connectors when MX points to a third-party service, inbound/outbound mail flow best practices).
6. Also check the "Pilot and deploy Defender for Endpoint" and "Pilot and deploy Defender for Cloud Apps" pages under learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/ for stated prerequisites/dependencies.

For each source report, in this format:
- Title, current URL, products covered.
- Order: does it give an explicit order (numbered steps or phases)? Yes/No (name the steps briefly if yes).
- Prerequisites: does it list prerequisites? Yes/No.
- 1–3 example dependencies it states, PARAPHRASED in your own words (no quotes longer than 10 words). Prefer cross-product ones (e.g. "Cloud Apps Conditional Access app control needs an Entra Conditional Access policy with session control"; "MDE device risk in Intune compliance needs the MDE–Intune connector first").
- Front matter: ms.topic and the original_content_git_url's repo name (e.g. MicrosoftDocs/defender-docs-pr), if you can get them.
Mark anything you could not verify. Keep the whole report under 800 words. Return it as your final message.

input.message:
**Sources for an M365 security dependency catalogue, beyond Entra (checked 2026-11-05)**

I read sources 1–3, 5, 6, the Purview information-protection page, Intune get-started, the repositories and the markdown endpoint myself. Four research subagents covered the rest. They read the pages live, but I did not re-read them. "O" means the source gives an explicit order and "P" means it lists prerequisites. All URLs start with learn.microsoft.com/en-us unless shown otherwise.

## Sources

**1. Zero Trust deployment plan with Microsoft 365.** Now at /security/zero-trust/microsoft-365-zero-trust (it moved from /microsoft-365/security/). Covers Entra, Intune, Defender XDR, Purview and AI.
- O: Yes. Five swim lanes; lane 1 has three phases.
- P: Yes, a Prerequisites column in each phase table.
- Starting-point access policies need no device enrollment.
- Register endpoints in Entra, then enroll them in Intune, before the enterprise-tier policies that require compliant devices.
- Purview work can start at any time.

**2. Zero Trust identity and device access.** The series is /security/zero-trust/zero-trust-identity-device-access-policies-overview, with -prerequisite (ms.topic is `checklist`), -common, -workloads and the guest-access page. Covers Entra, Intune, Exchange Online, SharePoint and Teams.
- O: Yes, as tiers: starting point, then enterprise, then specialized.
- P: Yes, a table per identity model with Exceptions and Licensing columns.
- Password hash sync is required even in federated tenants, because leaked-credential risk depends on it.
- Plan hybrid join or device registration before device-based Conditional Access (CA).
- SharePoint's unmanaged-device control creates an Entra CA policy automatically.
- Guests need their own MFA policy and must be excluded from compliance policies.

**3. Deploy your identity infrastructure for Microsoft 365.** /microsoft-365/enterprise/deploy-identity-solution-overview. Covers Entra and M365.
- O: Yes, four steps: identity model, privileged accounts, user accounts, deploy the model.
- P: No, only a licensing column.
- It calls itself the first layer of the Zero Trust stack.
- Create Entra groups for each protection level before assigning CA and Intune policies.

**4. Business Premium.** /microsoft-365/admin/security-and-compliance/m365b-security-best-practices (Top 10), /microsoft-365/business-premium/m365-business-premium-setup, and .../m365bp-devices-enrollment. The old security deployment guide returns 404.
- O: Yes. Setup goes domain, users, DNS, then security; device setup has six steps.
- P: Yes, on the devices page.
- Compliance policies do nothing until a device-based CA policy applies.
- Mark devices with no compliance policy as not compliant before turning on CA.

**5. Defender XDR pilot and deploy.** /defender-xdr/pilot-deploy-overview. Covers Defender for Identity (MDI), Office 365 (MDO), Endpoint (MDE) and Cloud Apps (MDCA).
- O: Yes, MDI, then MDO, then MDE, then MDCA. The page says this order is based on effort, so it is soft.
- P: Only on the component pages.
- From the MDCA pilot page: session policies need CA app control, which needs an Entra CA policy.

**6. Defender for Office 365.** /defender-office-365/mdo-deployment-guide. Covers MDO, Exchange Online and Entra.
- O: Yes, eight steps.
- P: Yes (roles).
- Set up SPF, then DKIM, then DMARC, explicitly in that order, for every custom domain including parked ones.
- User-reported messages need a dedicated reporting mailbox created first.
- Priority account protection requires tagging users at /microsoft-365/admin/setup/priority-accounts first (up to 250).
- When MX points to a third-party filter: turn on Enhanced Filtering on the inbound connector, then remove SCL -1 rules (Exchange enhanced-filtering page).

**7. Defender for Endpoint, Identity and Cloud Apps.** /defender-endpoint/mde-planning-guide (five steps), /defender-for-identity/deploy/deploy-defender-identity and deploy-sensor-v3, and /defender-cloud-apps/get-started (six steps).
- O: Yes. P: Yes.
- Activating an MDI v3 sensor from the portal needs the domain controller onboarded to MDE.
- MDCA blocking on endpoints needs MDE network protection in block mode.

**8. Intune and Windows.** Pages:
- Intune: /intune/fundamentals/get-started (five steps), planning-guide (seven steps), deploy-setup-step-1 (nine steps), /intune/device-enrollment/guide, and deploy-compliance-step-3 (dated 2023).
- Autopilot: /autopilot/requirements.
- Windows Hello for Business: /windows/security/identity-protection/hello-for-business/deploy/hybrid-cloud-kerberos-trust.
- LAPS: /intune/device-security/laps/overview and /entra/identity/devices/howto-manage-local-admin-passwords.

Findings:
- O: Yes for most; No for the Autopilot and LAPS overview pages. P: Yes.
- Set the MDM authority and assign licences before enrollment.
- Turn on Entra automatic MDM enrollment before Autopilot.
- Turn on LAPS in Entra device settings before the Intune LAPS policy (Entra-joined devices).
- Windows Hello cloud Kerberos trust needs the Entra Kerberos server object first.

**9. Purview.** Pages:
- /purview/information-protection-solution: O Yes but iterative; P licensing only.
- /purview/deploymentmodels/: "Secure by default" has four steps, and step 1 lists the switches to turn on first. A shadow-AI blueprint spans Purview, MDCA, Entra Internet Access and Intune.
- Labels: sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites and sensitivity-labels-sharepoint-onedrive-files.
- DLP: dlp-overview-plan-for-dlp (simulate, then policy tips, then enforce).
- Audit: audit-get-started (six steps).
- Insider Risk: insider-risk-management-configure (six steps).

Dependencies:
- Labels for groups and sites need Entra group-label support turned on, then a label sync.
- Insider Risk needs audit on, plus the HR connector or MDE integration depending on the template.

**10. Copilot.** /copilot/plan/secure-govern-copilot-foundational-deployment-guidance (the old oversharing blueprint redirects here; its PDF detail is unverified), /copilot/adopt/enablement-resources (five steps), /security/zero-trust/copilots/zero-trust-microsoft-365-copilot (seven steps, E3 then E5), and Copilot Studio /microsoft-copilot-studio/guidance/sec-gov-intro.
- Put SharePoint oversharing controls in place, then labels, before assigning Copilot licences.
- Copilot Studio governance zones rely on Power Platform managed environments and data policies.

**11. Secure collaboration and guests.** The M365 solution pages are now archived under /previous-versions/microsoft-365/solutions/... (dated 2023–24). Also /entra/architecture/secure-external-access-resources, an eight-article series.
- O: Yes, in the archived "Collaborate with guests in a team" page.
- The layers go Entra B2B, then Teams guest access, then Groups guest settings, then SharePoint organization sharing, then site sharing.
- A site cannot be more open than the organization level.
- Shared channels need the Teams setting plus Entra cross-tenant B2B direct connect.

**12. Teams and Exchange Online.** /microsoftteams/guest-access (P: Yes; no live checklist), /microsoftteams/trusted-organizations-external-meetings-chat, and the Exchange pages on Basic auth deprecation, SMTP AUTH and modern auth.
- External access works only when both the organization setting and the user policy allow it.
- Security defaults turns off SMTP AUTH.
- A CA policy that blocks legacy authentication also blocks certificate-based Exchange ActiveSync.

**13. Global Secure Access.** /entra/architecture/gsa-deployment-guide-intro, plus -internet-access, -private-access and -microsoft-traffic. Also /entra/global-secure-access/how-to-compliant-network and how-to-universal-tenant-restrictions.
- O: Yes. P: Yes.
- Devices must be joined or registered before the client is installed.
- Turn on Global Secure Access signaling for CA before the compliant-network policy.
- Universal tenant restrictions need the tenant restrictions v2 policies first.

**14. Power Platform.** /power-platform/guidance/adoption/secure-default-environment, admin-best-practices, /power-platform/admin/wp-data-loss-prevention and cross-tenant-restrictions.
- O: Partial; sequenced but not numbered. P: No.
- Sharing limits need managed environments.
- No single ordered security baseline exists.

**15. Exposure Management and Secure Score.** /security-exposure-management/initiatives-list and /defender-xdr/microsoft-secure-score-improvement-actions.
- O: No; both are ranked by risk.
- P: Free text only. Each initiative lists the workloads it requires; a Secure Score action's Implementation section names licences or other actions to do first.
- The Graph secureScoreControlProfile resource has no prerequisite field (it has tier, implementationCost, userImpact, threats and remediation HTML).

**16. Zero Trust Workshop and Assessment.** microsoft.github.io/zerotrustassessment; repo microsoft/zerotrustassessment (MIT).
- O: Partial. Pillars run Identity, Devices, Data, Network, and so on. Within a pillar, the order is only the left-to-right position of tasks in ZeroTrustTemplate.xlsx, with no arrows.
- P: No field. About 1,100 task .md files; prerequisites are in the prose.
- ztw-task-mapping.json maps assessment tests to workshop tasks.

**17. CISA SCuBA.** cisagov/ScubaGear baselines, v2.0.0 (CC0). securitysuite.md replaces defender.md, and there is a draft si.md for AI.
- O: No.
- P: No per-policy section. Each group has License Requirements and Implementation sections; si.md adds a governance prerequisites group.
- Policy IDs sit in HTML comments, so they can be parsed.

**18. ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud.** blueprint.asd.gov.au; source on GitHub at ASD-Blueprint/ASD-Blueprint-for-Secure-Cloud (CC BY 4.0, with exceptions).
- O: No. P: Free text and footnotes only.
- Entra device identities are a prerequisite for device-based CA and for Intune.
- Its M365DSC files have no DependsOn.

**19. CIS Microsoft 365 v7.0.0.**
- O: No; sections follow the admin centres.
- P: No prerequisite field. Licence needs show only through the E3/E5 profiles. Other dependencies appear only implicitly in the Impact, Audit and Remediation text. I checked the structure only.

## Public docs repositories (checked with gh)

**Public:**
- **MicrosoftDocs/microsoft-365-docs:** CC BY 4.0, default branch `public`. Its copilot/ folder stopped updating on 2026-04-30 (stale). Its security/ folder is almost empty.
- **MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs:** the LICENSE file is **MIT, not CC BY**; I checked both LICENSE and LICENSE-CODE. It includes Global Secure Access and the architecture deployment plans.
- **CC BY 4.0:** power-platform, azure-docs, office-docs-powershell (cmdlet reference), OfficeDocs-SharePoint-PowerShell, msteams-docs (Teams developer docs only) and m365copilot-docs (extensibility only).
- **Archived:** CloudAppSecurityDocs.

**Not public.** gh cannot resolve these; their names come from each page's `original_content_git_url`:
- defender-docs-pr (all Defender products, including Defender for Cloud)
- security-pr (Zero Trust)
- memdocs-pr (Intune and Autopilot)
- Purview-pr
- OfficeDocs-SkypeForBusiness-pr (Teams admin)
- OfficeDocs-SharePoint-pr
- OfficeDocs-Exchange-pr
- copilot-pr
- windows-docs-pr
- businessapps-copilot-docs-pr
- officearchive-pr

These pages fall only under the Learn terms of use; I could not confirm a CC BY licence for them.

## Structured fields

- **Markdown endpoint (verified):** any Learn page requested with `Accept: text/markdown` returns markdown with YAML front matter (content-type text/markdown). That makes the private-source products mineable without their repositories.
- **Front matter** includes `ms.topic` (values seen: checklist, solution-overview, get-started, install-set-up-deploy, best-practice), `ms.collection` (m365solution-*, zerotrust-solution), `ms.date`, `updated_at` and `original_content_git_url`.
- **Headings:** there are `## Prerequisites` headings in about 2,920 entra-docs files, 140 power-platform files and 76 microsoft-365-docs files (GitHub code-search counts, approximate). Other common headings are "Before you begin", "Requirements" and numbered "## Step N".
- **Tables:** Zero Trust pages use fixed-column prerequisite tables (Includes / Prerequisites / Doesn't include; Configuration / Exceptions / Licensing).
- **Images:** the order diagrams (swim lanes, the Defender pilot flow) are images, so their order is not in the text.

## Top 10 sources for a cross-product catalogue

1. **Zero Trust identity and device access series:** the only set that tables Entra, Intune, Exchange, SharePoint and Teams prerequisites for CA.
2. **Zero Trust deployment plan:** the backbone order across Entra, Intune, Defender and Purview.
3. **Purview deployment models:** numbered steps with "turn on first" switches across Purview, SharePoint, Entra, MDCA, Intune and Global Secure Access.
4. **Zero Trust for Copilot:** seven steps across six products, all required before licences are assigned.
5. **Archived guest-collaboration pages:** the clearest layered order from Entra B2B through Groups and Teams to SharePoint.
6. **Insider Risk get-started:** depends on audit, the HR connector, DLP, MDE and MDCA.
7. **Defender XDR pilot series:** component order plus the MDE–MDCA and MDCA–Entra CA links.
8. **Global Secure Access guides:** device identity, client, traffic profiles, CA signaling and tenant restrictions.
9. **Zero Trust Workshop repo:** machine-readable tasks and test mapping (MIT).
10. **Intune get-started plus the MDE–Intune integration page:** the device side of the CA chain.

## Cross-product dependencies a product-by-product reading would miss

1. **Password hash sync:** needed even in federated tenants, because leaked-credential risk depends on it (Zero Trust prerequisite page).
2. **Device risk in Intune compliance:** turn on the Intune connection in Defender advanced features first, then the Intune toggles. A require-compliant CA policy then uses that risk. Source: /intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/configure-integration.
3. **Labels for groups and sites:** need Entra group-label support and a label sync. The label's unmanaged-device option does nothing without a SharePoint app-enforced-restrictions CA policy (Purview containers page).
4. **SharePoint/OneDrive label support:** must be on before DLP, eDiscovery or auto-labeling can read encrypted files (Purview SharePoint labels page).
5. **Insider Risk templates:** security-violation templates need MDE onboarding plus the Insider Risk toggle in Defender. Data-leak templates need DLP policies set to High severity (Insider Risk get-started).
6. **MDCA session controls:** need an Entra CA policy using app control, with the app added to Entra first (MDCA pilot page).
7. **Teams guests:** work only once Entra B2B, the Groups guest settings and SharePoint organization sharing all allow them (archived guest pages).
8. **Power Platform outbound mail:** the Outlook connector cannot be blocked, so Exchange mail-flow rules on Power Automate headers have to stop outbound mail from flows (secure-default-environment).
9. **Security defaults:** turning them on disables SMTP AUTH, so the choice between security defaults and CA decides the Exchange client-auth settings (Exchange SMTP AUTH page).
10. **MDI v3 sensors:** activating them from the portal needs the domain controller onboarded to MDE (MDI v3 page).

## Not verified

- The detailed activities in the Copilot foundational guidance PDF.
- Whether an API exists for Exposure Management initiatives.
- What is inside each Secure Score action's remediation HTML.
- The licence on content whose source repo is private.
- The exact GitHub search counts.
- Pages that only the subagents read (items 4, 7–19).

## Structured fields

- **Markdown endpoint (verified):** any Learn page requested with `Accept: text/markdown` returns markdown with YAML front matter (content-type text/markdown). That makes the private-source products mineable without their repositories.
- **Front matter** includes `ms.topic` (values seen: checklist, solution-overview, get-started, install-set-up-deploy, best-practice), `ms.collection` (m365solution-*, zerotrust-solution), `ms.date`, `updated_at` and `original_content_git_url`.
- **Headings:** there are `## Prerequisites` headings in about 2,920 entra-docs files, 140 power-platform files and 76 microsoft-365-docs files (GitHub code-search counts, approximate). Other common headings are "Before you begin", "Requirements" and numbered "## Step N".
- **Tables:** Zero Trust pages use fixed-column prerequisite tables (Includes / Prerequisites / Doesn't include; Configuration / Exceptions / Licensing).
- **Images:** the order diagrams (swim lanes, the Defender pilot flow) are images, so their order is not in the text.

## Top 10 sources for a cross-product catalogue

1. **Zero Trust identity and device access series:** the only set that tables Entra, Intune, Exchange, SharePoint and Teams prerequisites for CA.
2. **Zero Trust deployment plan:** the backbone order across Entra, Intune, Defender and Purview.
3. **Purview deployment models:** numbered steps with "turn on first" switches across Purview, SharePoint, Entra, MDCA, Intune and Global Secure Access.
4. **Zero Trust for Copilot:** seven steps across six products, all required before licences are assigned.
5. **Archived guest-collaboration pages:** the clearest layered order from Entra B2B through Groups and Teams to SharePoint.
6. **Insider Risk get-started:** depends on audit, the HR connector, DLP, MDE and MDCA.
7. **Defender XDR pilot series:** component order plus the MDE–MDCA and MDCA–Entra CA links.
8. **Global Secure Access guides:** device identity, client, traffic profiles, CA signaling and tenant restrictions.
9. **Zero Trust Workshop repo:** machine-readable tasks and test mapping (MIT).
10. **Intune get-started plus the MDE–Intune integration page:** the device side of the CA chain.

## Cross-product dependencies a product-by-product reading would miss

1. **Password hash sync:** needed even in federated tenants, because leaked-credential risk depends on it (Zero Trust prerequisite page).
2. **Device risk in Intune compliance:** turn on the Intune connection in Defender advanced features first, then the Intune toggles. A require-compliant CA policy then uses that risk. Source: /intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/configure-integration.
3. **Labels for groups and sites:** need Entra group-label support and a label sync. The label's unmanaged-device option does nothing without a SharePoint app-enforced-restrictions CA policy (Purview containers page).
4. **SharePoint/OneDrive label support:** must be on before DLP, eDiscovery or auto-labeling can read encrypted files (Purview SharePoint labels page).
5. **Insider Risk templates:** security-violation templates need MDE onboarding plus the Insider Risk toggle in Defender. Data-leak templates need DLP policies set to High severity (Insider Risk get-started).
6. **MDCA session controls:** need an Entra CA policy using app control, with the app added to Entra first (MDCA pilot page).
7. **Teams guests:** work only once Entra B2B, the Groups guest settings and SharePoint organization sharing all allow them (archived guest pages).
8. **Power Platform outbound mail:** the Outlook connector cannot be blocked, so Exchange mail-flow rules on Power Automate headers have to stop outbound mail from flows (secure-default-environment).
9. **Security defaults:** turning them on disables SMTP AUTH, so the choice between security defaults and CA decides the Exchange client-auth settings (Exchange SMTP AUTH page).
10. **MDI v3 sensors:** activating them from the portal needs the domain controller onboarded to MDE (MDI v3 page).
